name: Rethink Priorities
story: $1,000 of research changes where **{animal-welfare: 1000 * share * moved_per_dollar|$}** of funders' money goes in animal welfare and **{global-health-and-development: 1000 * share * moved_per_dollar|$}** in global health.
summary: A research organisation that helps funders and charities decide where money does most good across animal welfare, global health and catastrophic risks: research and coordination for animal advocates and funders, commissioned global health research for foundations such as Gates and Packard, cross-cause prioritisation and moral-weight work, and surveys for effective-giving organisations. It also fiscally sponsors other projects (Apollo Research, Epoch, the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy and others), whose spending is theirs, not paid for by a gift to Rethink Priorities.

spending.source: https://rethinkpriorities.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Signed-Final-Report-and-Financial-Statements.pdf (Rethink Priorities, audited consolidated statements, year to 31 December 2025, CliftonLarsonAllen: programme services $19,065,433, of which its fiscally sponsored and incubated projects $15,649,319 (Form 990 Part III lines 4a Special Projects $11,744,046 and 4b the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy $3,905,273, https://rethinkpriorities.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/RP-12-31-2025-Form_990-NoSchedB.pdf). The projects' spending is paid from money restricted to them and is theirs (Epoch AI and the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy have their own models on this site), so the programme here is its own four research departments, $3,416,114. Management and general $2,698,458, fundraising $639,031.)
